summary: Giovanni Gentile (1875–1944) was an Italian philosopher. Educated at Liceo Ximenes, Scuola Normale Superiore, and the University of Florence, he held posts at Palermo, Pisa, Rome, Scuola Normale Superiore, Bocconi University, and served as president of IsMEO.

Giovanni Vacca (1872–1953) was an Italian sinologist and historian. He studied at the University of Genoa and held academic posts at the University of Florence (~1911–1921) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1923–1947), teaching scholars including Giuseppe Tucci.

Giovanni Verardi (born 1947) is an Italian scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Allahabad, Banaras Hindu University, and Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, and held a post at Kyoto University.

Girindrasekhar Bose (1887–1953) studied at Presidency University, Medical College Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He worked at Medical College Kolkata (1911–1915) and was Professor of Experimental Psychology at the University of Calcutta (1917–1949).

Gisho Nakano (1891–1977) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Koyasan University and Kyushu University (~1925–1954), where he taught Shingen Takagi.
Giuliana Martini is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. In 2010, she held posts at both the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Kyoto University.

Giuseppe Bardelli (1815–1865) was an Italian scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien, and served as Dozent for Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (~1845–1859).

Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti (1774–1849) was an Italian linguist. He studied at the University of Bologna (~1786–1797) and subsequently held an academic post there from around 1797 to 1831, teaching Giuseppe Bardelli.

Giuseppe Tucci (1894–1984) studied at Rome, Calcutta, and Visva-Bharati. A specialist in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, he held posts at the University of Calcutta, Sapienza University of Rome, and served as president of IsMEO.

Giuseppe Vignato is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies at Peking University under Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Su Bai, and Shichang Ma, and held a post there (attested 2017).

Giyu Nishi (1897–1993) studied Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo under Takakusu, Kimura, Anesaki, Nagai, Ui, Kato, and Lévi. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1926) and as professor at Toyo University (1927).
Gnanawimala Chandima is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Godabarish Mishra (1886–1956) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Ravenshaw College (~1906–1910) and the University of Calcutta (~1910–1912), and later served as Director at the University of Madras.

Gombojab Tsybikov (1873–1930) was a scholar of Tibetology and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University and Saint Petersburg State University, and later served as Lecturer of the Mongolian Language at Far Eastern Federal University (~1902–1917).

Gopinath Kaviraj (1887–1976) was an Indian scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Allahabad (~1910–1914) and served as Professor of Tantra-Śāstra at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1964–1969).

Gordon D. Kaufman (1925–2011) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Northwestern University (~1947–1948) and Yale Divinity School (~1948–1955), and held a faculty post at Harvard University from around 1963 to 1995.
Gordon Johnson (born 1943) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1961–1967) and held a post at the University of Cambridge (attested 2012).

Gottfried Hermann (1772–1848) was a German linguist. He studied at Leipzig University (~1786–1793) and the University of Jena (~1793–1794), and subsequently held a post at Leipzig University from around 1798 to 1848.

Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer (1694–1738), a sinologist and historian, studied at the University of Königsberg under Christoph Theodosius Walther. He held posts at Königsberg and the Russian Academy of Sciences (from 1726) for classical antiquities and oriental languages.

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner (1840–1899) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at King's College London in 1858, held a post there in 1861, and later worked at the Oriental Institute in Woking (~1889–1899).
